title: Search a 2D Matrix
kidExplanation: A matrix where each row is sorted and rows increase. Treat it like one long sorted list.
plainProblem: Search a 2D Matrix: A matrix where each row is sorted and rows increase. Worked example — input: matrix = [[1,3,5,7],[10,11,16,20],[23,30,34,60]], target = 3; expected output: true. Why: Found. Interview pattern to name out loud: Binary search (halving the range).

thinkingSteps.title: Brute force idea
thinkingSteps.body: For “Search a 2D Matrix”, first say a correct slow approach: scan or retry every candidate until the example works by hand. Input matrix = [[1,3,5,7],[10,11,16,20],[23,30,34,60]], target = 3 should still produce true.

thinkingSteps.title: Why it is slow
thinkingSteps.body: Count the nested work. If each choice restarts a full scan, time blows up. Name the cost before optimizing — interviewers want that honesty. Target after the insight: O(log(m*n).

thinkingSteps.title: Aha insight
thinkingSteps.body: Since both the rows and columns in the input 2D matrix are sorted, we can treat the matrix as a one-dimensional sorted array and perform binary search to find the target element. We can map the 2D indices to the corresponding index in the 1D array and then apply binary search to locate the target element.

thinkingSteps.title: Better idea
thinkingSteps.body: Commit to Binary search (halving the range). Sorted data or a monotonic yes/no answer. Walk example `matrix = [[1,3,5,7],[10,11,16,20],[23,30,34,60]], target = 3` → `true` while naming each variable, then code. Close with O(log(m*n) time and O(1) space.
